title: Eight active USGS first-forecast regions show no clear magnitude trend on days 1 to 30
abstract: We tested whether recorded magnitudes change with time in the regions of first USGS generic aftershock forecasts. We used a fixed ComCat and forecast snapshot and a conditional permutation test that removes productivity, decay shape and the fixed magnitude distribution. The sample has 192 forecasts and 335 counted records on days 1 to 30. Eight regions have at least five events. None rejected magnitude-time independence after Holm correction; all primary adjusted p values were 1. A type-controlled test also gave no rejection. Puerto Rico supplied 157 records. Its late versus early odds ratio for magnitudes at least 3.95 was 0.774, with an exact 95% interval of 0.355 to 1.660. An uncorrected issue-start trend disappeared when shuffles held magnitude type fixed. The null results leave the source of earlier timing failures unresolved. We also show why time-dependent detection that acts equally across magnitudes can change a time curve without changing this test. Small samples, mixed magnitude scales, revised records and nonmonotone effects limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate tests, checks and a figure are included; external earthquake records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Primary time-magnitude rank correlations for eight active forecast regions. Type-controlled scores use ranks centered within preferred magnitude type. None of the individual tests passes Holm correction.
